acceptance_criteria.evidence: The webhook URL is an operator-managed GitHub Actions secret and this candidate neither reads nor commits it.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Required issuer verification/runtime configuration is present without committing secrets.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: The shim strips publication and governance authority credentials before model execution, creates a private credential home, disables inherited OpenCode plugins, and supplies a deny-by-default inline permission policy without committing any secret value.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Exact authorized test event passes GitHub trigger -> issuer authorization -> canonical Smart Prompt build/handoff boundary.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: The final end-to-end trigger/issuer/handoff proof is an operational validation after this candidate is merged and deployed. The exact candidate itself is covered by hosted CI, trusted preflight, CodeQL, and governance admission.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Missing/invalid authorization or endpoint configuration still fails closed.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: The shim rejects unknown or incomplete sandbox argv, unexpected binds, invalid workspace/home roots, untrusted executable locations, and any provider command other than `opencode run`; all such cases return failure rather than falling back to unrestricted execution.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: No autonomous merge/deploy side effect occurs from the validation event.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: The shim only executes OpenCode against the isolated attempt clone. It strips GitHub publication credentials and all GIT_* variables; commit signing, push, rollback, merge, and deployment remain outside the model process in the trusted parent runtime.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Issue #437 can then be re-authorized through the canonical governed trigger.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Re-authorizing Issue #437 is the next operator action after #441 passes its deployed end-to-end validation; this candidate supplies the Railway-compatible runtime prerequisite only.

defect_families.evidence: No caller-controlled timestamp, cutoff, or historical-state selection is introduced; sandbox admission is determined only from the exact argv and filesystem locations supplied by the trusted parent.
The shim does not perform validate-then-persist logic. It validates the complete sandbox contract before spawning the provider and never writes governed persistent state.
No durable identity is accepted from model or caller content; executable and workspace identities are derived from trusted parent paths and exact mount declarations.
Missing or malformed authority/runtime declarations fail closed: unsupported options, missing binds, invalid roots, or untrusted executable locations raise SandboxShimError.
No secondary durable carrier is added. Model-visible state is confined to the isolated clone and private credential home, while publication credentials are removed.
No ordering or clock promise is introduced. Validation is deterministic over the exact argv and path topology.
Authorization and publication proofs are not re-aimable: the provider receives neither GitHub push credentials nor governance signing/runtime authority variables.
Unexpected bind mappings and executable locations are rejected; the shim accepts only system read-only mounts and the pinned /app/bin executable mapping expected from Hunter.
This candidate uses the connector ingress with an exact authorization receipt; review and receipt evidence paths remain excluded from the substantive change set by trusted admission logic.
Connector admission authenticates the authorized connector channel rather than treating unsigned API commits as ordinary pre-push provenance; the exact receipt is bound to this branch and base.
The candidate’s substantive change set is exact and complete (one source module plus its focused tests); evidence artifacts cannot strand or conceal an implementation transition.
The connector authorization receipt is re-derived against the exact source/test blobs and current main base, with review/receipt artifacts treated as evidence rather than implementation scope.
This pre-ready hostile review is refreshed against the exact candidate content before Ready consideration and covers the governing Issue criteria plus recurring-defect families.
No pending check is represented as success in this review. Hosted exact-head CI/trusted preflight results are independently published by GitHub workflows.
Claims here are tied to concrete code paths and focused tests: strict argv parsing, credential stripping, isolated root checks, and deny-by-default permissions.
All hosted validation and review state is bound to the exact candidate head; any later content mutation makes this review stale and forces a refresh.
The runtime boundary is explicit: untrusted model execution is separated from trusted commit signing, publication, rollback, and exact-head validation.

The permission policy defaults every OpenCode capability to deny and selectively allows only project read/edit/glob/grep/LSP operations; shell, web, tasks, skills, questions, and external-directory access remain denied.

Railway’s non-privileged namespace limitation is handled without requesting privileged container capabilities; the provider runs in the existing service with credentials stripped and the model constrained to the isolated attempt clone.

findings.evidence: Railway rejects bubblewrap namespace creation. The candidate replaces only that unavailable kernel isolation step with a strict fail-closed argv shim while preserving the isolated attempt clone and trusted parent publication boundary.
Provider credential exposure is blocked: GitHub push credentials, governance/runtime authority variables, HUNTER_PROMPT_* and GIT_* values are removed before OpenCode starts.
Capability escape is blocked by OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT with `* = deny` and an allowlist limited to read/edit/glob/grep/LSP, plus `--pure` and Claude-plugin disablement.

This application-level sandbox is intentionally weaker than an OS namespace boundary; final deployed #441 validation must confirm OpenCode honors the pinned permission contract on Railway before #437 is re-authorized.
